# Education in Sweden
Sweden's education system encompasses preschool, compulsory schooling (grundskola), upper secondary education (gymnasieskola), and higher education. Preschool is available from age one and is free for all children from age three for at least three hours a day, with fees for additional hours based on family income. Compulsory education lasts for nine years, from ages 6/7 to 15/16, and includes a wide curriculum of core academic subjects; students receive grades from year 6 onward, using a scale from A to F. After completing compulsory school, students may enter upper secondary school, which lasts three years and is divided into 18 national programmes (academic preparatory or vocational), with admission based on grades from compulsory schooling; approximately 99% of students enroll.
Higher education in Sweden follows the Bologna Process, with undergraduate (Bachelor’s), graduate (Master’s), and doctoral levels offered at universities and university colleges. Admission requires completion of upper secondary school and demonstrated proficiency in Swedish and English. Sweden also offers higher vocational education focused on practical, subject-specific training, independent from the traditional university system. Public funding supports both public and independent (free) schools, with independent schools accounting for a significant—though debated—portion of student enrollment. Swedish education is notable for its inclusivity, flexibility, and strong emphasis on equal access, although recent reforms and debates address grading standards, profit-making in independent schools, and performance on international assessments such as PISA and PIRLS.
